newsitem.title: USA: Destec shareholders approve NGC merger.
newsitem.headline: Destec shareholders approve NGC merger.

text.p: Destec Energy Inc shareholders on Wednesday approved a $1.27 billion merger with NGC Corp and executives said the deal remained on track to close later this month pending federal approval.

Once the deal closes, NGC plans to operate Destec as the generating arm of its power business, and will rebuild its international power operations and expand its domestic generating capacity, NGC President Tom Matthews said.
"We will very quickly use (Destec) for an international platform with an initial focus on the Americas and Europe," Matthews told Reuters after Destec's shareholder meeting in Houston.

In the merger, NGC will add to its power portfolio $300 million in assets and 1,800 megawatts of domestic generation from 20 power plants centered largely in California and Texas. NGC will sell off non-core assets including a 220 megawatt power plant to Florida Power Corp for $445 million, five international power plants with 950 megawatt capacity to AES Corp for $407 million and $44 million in lignite reserves to Destec majority shareholder Dow Chemical Co.

After the merger closes, Destec will be seeded with about $50 million to $75 million in project financing from NGC for worldwide power investments to expand its generating capacity both for firm contract power sales and wholesale trading by NGC's power trading arm, Matthews said.
The deal still must be approved by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, which meets twice more this month, he said.

Destec has not been sitting idle waiting for the deal to close. The company has opened a trading center in San Francisco to sell power to commercial and industrial customers once the market is opened in early 1998, and NGC executive Dan Ryser has been working out of offices at the Houston-based company to coordinate the merger.
Destec was formed in 1989 as subsidiary of Dow Chemical, which controlled 80 percent of Destec shares and signalled plans to vote in favor of the merger when it was announced in February.

Before the merger, Destec had been projecting after-tax profits of $63 million this year, $94.9 million next year and $108.2 million in 1999. Chairman Charles Goff said the company still expects "potentially explosive growth" following the merger.
"The deal will be slightly accretive this year for both earnings and cash flow," NGC's Matthews said.

Of Destec's 670 employees, about 450 will remain with NGC and about 10 percent will be laid off. The remainder will go to companies buying assets being spun off by NGC when the deal closes, Matthews said.
